sequencing_rationale: Group A first (flow edits): each row is a distinct file or directory-paired pair, no two rows touch the same file — zero merge conflict within Group A even if agent-father were paused/resumed.

Within Group A: ordered by call-graph dependency (PO entry → PM mid → developer → QA → agent-father self → dev-team drain). Self-wiring (row 6) lands BEFORE dev-team drain (row 7) so agent-father's own heartbeat instrumentation is active before it touches the cross-cutting drain flow.

Group B (tool-package batch) last: only after all flow edits land, because tool-package additions are advertisement-only — they must reflect the actually-wired flows. If Group B preceded Group A, packages would advertise tools agents have not yet invoked.
No .ts changes expected in 1960c — Phase 1 already shipped the MCP tools. If 1960a discovers a missing .ts edit, escalate back to PO before agent-father picks up.
Backward-compat with HEAD.lock preflight (per PO signal constraints): both stay in place; HEAD.lock prevents same-session git race, task-lock prevents 2-session race.
